title: Count the votes
prompt: `CountVotes(List<string> votes)` receives one candidate name per vote. It should return a dictionary with each name as a key and the number of votes it got as the value. The starter stores 1 for every name, however often it appears.
hints: What should happen the second time the loop meets the same name?
A name that is already a key needs its old value plus 1. A new name starts at 1.
Use ContainsKey to choose between counts[vote] = counts[vote] + 1 and counts[vote] = 1.
checkLabels: Ana appears twice, so her count must be 2.
Ben appears once, so his count must be 1.
Two different names must give two keys.
An empty list must give an empty dictionary.
A name that appears three times must have a count of 3.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Reads a key before it has been added.
Starts a new name at 0, so every count is one short.

feedback: Trace the dictionary by hand for the failing list. Write down the value under each key after every run of the loop.
